Stage 1 reference: Firmware and tuning

What the firmware does, the bring-up and tuning notes, and the known risks of the design.

ReferenceThis page is detail behind the Stage 1 guide. You can build without reading it: each step of the guide links to the section it needs when something goes wrong. Like everything in Tailwhip, it is designed and simulated, not built.

Firmware

firmware/stage1_balance/stage1_balance.ino, board "ESP32 Dev Module". No radio, no laptop in the loop. It reads the wheel sensor on GPIO 34 if one is plugged in and working, and runs on the IMU alone if not.

  • 400 Hz loop: read the IMU, complementary filter for pitch, PID, one PWM pair to the MX1508.
  • Arms itself when held within 5 degrees of upright for half a second; lets go past 22 degrees.
  • Serial at 115200: gains, trim, direction flip, save to flash, a 50 Hz CSV stream, an open-loop motor test, edit imu|ir to pick which gain set to change, wnl for the motor's no-load speed, wheel auto|off, and ir / irw 1 to watch the sensor.
  • Default gains come from sim.py tune (per rad, rad/s, m/s, m). IMU only: kp 1.62, kd 0.37, kv 2.42, kx 0.137. With the sensor: kp 1.79, kd 0.30, kv 2.09, kx 0.54. Both assume a no-load wheel speed of 21 rad/s (200 rpm).
  • The filter, the PID and the wheel-sensor code are the same code path sim.py simulates. Change one, change the other.

Bring-up

  1. Set the Mini360 to 5.0 V on the bench before it touches the ESP32.
  2. Flash, open the serial monitor, type show. Tilt it forward: pitch must go positive.
  3. Wheels off the ground, motor 0.3 1000. The wheels must turn the way that would drive it forward; if not, dir -1. Count turns in a motor 1 3000 run to get the no-load speed (with the sensor fitted the sketch prints it), then wnl <rad/s> and save.
  4. Hold it upright and still through power-on (gyro calibration), then let it arm in your hands.
  5. Tune: creeps one way, change trim; falls over slowly, raise kp; shakes hard, lower kd; runs away, raise kv. save when it stands. Gains apply to the set picked with edit imu|ir; wheel off tunes milestone A with the sensor still plugged in.
  6. stream 1, log 20 s, and compare the wobble with out/plot_nominal.png.

Risks

  1. Narrow track. 52 mm between wheel centres; it tips sideways past about 20 degrees of roll. Flat floor only.
  2. Estimates. Stall torque (0.08 N m), no-load speed (200 rpm), slop (5 degrees) and dead zone are guesses until bench step 3. The torque sweep shows the result is sensitive to the first.
  3. Cheek plates. The core is 2.3 mm thick where it passes between the gearbox and each wheel, and 1.7 mm under the ring on the left.
  4. Position hold is loose. One wheel sensor has no direction, so expect about 25 cm of wander a minute. The sensor also comes off its module onto a pigtail, which is fiddly soldering, and the black ring needs enough infrared contrast against the wheel.
  5. No steering. Both wheels are on one shaft. It goes where it is pointed.
  6. Wheel fit. Each wheel sits on 5.5 mm of a 9.1 mm stub; check for wobble.
  7. Motor driver margin. The MX1508's weaker channel is rated below the simulated current peaks; see docs/electronics.md for the stronger channel and fallback boards.
